headline: Check Parks Canada Entry and Site Reservations
reservation: Daily entry fees apply and can typically be paid at gatehouses, though peak summer weekends may see capacity limits. Overnight stays in campgrounds, oTENTiks, or backcountry sites require separate reservations through the Parks Canada national system. System opening dates vary annually, so verify current booking windows on the official website before travel.

days.title: Waterways and Winding Ridges

stops.name: Le Passage Lookout
stops.detail: Pause at this elevated platform for a panoramic view of the narrowest section of Lake Wapizagonke carved by glacial activity.

stops.name: Shewenegan Picnic Area
stops.detail: Access the cascades or rent a canoe to explore the southern reaches of the park's interconnected lake system.

days.driving: Allow 1–2 hours for the Parkway; conditions vary with seasonal traffic.
days.note: The Promenade Parkway is the single main artery; expect slow speeds due to steep grades and cycling traffic.

days.title: Ancient Forests and Cascades

stops.name: Les Cascades Trail
stops.detail: Walk the accessible boardwalks surrounding these gentle falls, a popular spot for observing the local Laurentian shield geology.

stops.name: Lac À la Pêche
stops.detail: Visit the eastern sector for a quieter atmosphere and access to a network of multi-use forest trails.

days.driving: Allow 45 minutes from the gateway; conditions vary.
days.note: Morning starts are suggested to secure space at the more popular picnic and launch sites.

days.title: The Northern Wilderness Interface

stops.name: Le Belvédère de l'Île-aux-Pins
stops.detail: A short but steep trek leads to an iconic view of the pine-studded islands within Lake Wapizagonke.

stops.name: Rivière à la Pêche Service Centre
stops.detail: Utilize the interpretive displays to understand the park's transition from a logging territory to a protected conservation area.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for interior transit; conditions vary.
days.note: Verify the status of the Saint-Mathieu entrance as it may have different seasonal operating hours than Saint-Jean-des-Piles.

intel.title: Lot Capacity
intel.text: Parking at popular trailheads like Les Cascades fills quickly during summer holidays and autumn leaf-peeping weekends. Have an alternative stop planned in case your primary choice is at capacity.

intel.title: Connectivity Limits
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly unreliable or non-existent once you move past the main gatehouses into the park interior. Download offline maps and official park guides before departing from Shawinigan.

intel.title: Gateway Refueling
intel.text: There are no fuel stations located within the park boundaries. Ensure your tank is sufficient for a 120km round trip before leaving Shawinigan or Saint-Jean-des-Piles.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The Parkway typically closes to vehicles during the winter months, transitioning to a cross-country ski network. Check the official Parks Canada 'Bulletins' page for exact spring opening and autumn closing dates.

intel.title: Entrance Selection
intel.text: The park has two primary entrances; Saint-Jean-des-Piles is better for the scenic drive, while Saint-Mathieu offers quicker access to specific recreation areas. Confirm which gate is open during shoulder seasons.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at YQB and stop in Shawinigan for groceries and supplies before proceeding to the Saint-Jean-des-Piles entrance for check-in.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for the Parkway; RVs should check length restrictions for certain secondary parking areas.
plan.goldenHour: Le Passage Lookout offers expansive western views, though timing for the best light varies significantly between summer and autumn.
